title: Teens Try to Change the World, One Purchase at a Time
description: 完整答案表、全文段落速覽，以及逐題 Skim、Scan、Read、同義改寫與中伏位分析。

questions.translation: 透過購買選擇來改變世界，最初是從甚麼開始？

blocks.text: “Trying to change the world through what people purchase began with…”
“Eating morally, as some describe it, is becoming a priority for teenagers as well as adults in their early 20s.”
有些人稱之為「有道德地飲食」；這正成為青少年和二十出頭成年人重視的事情。
“Their peers on another 300 campuses are pushing to follow suit, according to Students United for Fair Trade in Washington, D.C.”
根據華盛頓特區 Students United for Fair Trade 的說法，另有 300 個校園的同齡學生也正推動仿效。
只看首尾句，這段會講校園消費 activism 如何在 food and beverage industries 出現及擴展。題目問 began with，所以要看這段開頭後面的歷史來源。
“What began a decade ago as a campaign on college campuses to avoid clothing made in overseas sweatshops has given birth to a parallel phenomenon in the food and beverage industries.”
十年前在大學校園開始的一場運動，是避免購買海外血汗工廠製造的衣服；它後來催生了 food and beverage industries 中類似的現象。
這句的主體是 “What began a decade ago as a campaign…”；真正回答 “began with” 的部分是：
“to avoid clothing made in overseas sweatshops”
避免購買海外血汗工廠製造的衣服。
所以，購買選擇作為道德行動，最初不是 coffee，也不是 chocolate，而是 clothing。
A chocolate：Paragraph 4 才說 Equal Exchange 後來推出 cocoa 和 chocolate bars，時間較後。
B clothing：正確，對應 “avoid clothing made in overseas sweatshops”。
C coffee：Paragraph 2 後半說 Fair Trade coffee 在校園推廣，但原文說 coffee 是 food and beverage industries 中的 parallel phenomenon，不是最初起點。

questions.translation: Bon Appétit 在 2006 年有多少間大學使用其服務？

blocks.text: “Bon Appétit had ______ colleges using its services in 2006.”
“‘Prior to that, students were excited to be getting sugared cereal.’”
在那之前，學生只因能吃到含糖 cereal 而感到興奮。
只看首尾句，可以估計這段說 ethical food concern 從 Fair Trade coffee 擴展到更全面的food-service choices。Bon Appétit 是這段主體，所以 Question 28 會定位到這裡。
原文沒有直接出現 2006，但有時間線：
“Though Bon Appétit intentionally limits its growth, its collegiate client list has grown from 58 to 71 in that period.”
雖然 Bon Appétit 有意限制自己的增長，但在那段期間，它的大學客戶名單由 58 增至 71。
題目問 2006 年有多少 colleges using its services。原文說自 2001 年以來，每年有超過 25 間college 邀請 Bon Appétit 競投 food-service contracts；接著說 client list 在那段時間由 58 增至 71。
因為題目給 2006，這正好是 2001 後五年左右，對應原文 “in that period” 和 “last five years”。所以到該時點的最新 client list 是 71。
A 25：這是每年邀請公司競投合約的 colleges 數量，不是已使用服務的 client list。
C 71：正確，對應 “has grown from 58 to 71”。

questions.translation: 買 Ethos Water 會幫助哪一類項目提供資金？

blocks.text: “Buying Ethos Water helps provide money for…”
“Wanting to ameliorate the world’s big problems can be frustrating, especially for those who feel ineffective because they are young.”
想改善世界上的大問題可能令人沮喪，尤其是對那些因年紀小而覺得自己沒有影響力的人。
“‘Buying products or supporting companies that give them ways to support global issues is one way for them to get involved, and they really appreciate that.’”
購買產品或支持能讓他們參與全球議題的公司，是他們投入其中的一種方式，而他們非常欣賞這一點。
這段講產品如何讓年輕人感到自己正在參與世界問題。Ethos Water 是中間例子。
“His example: Ethos Water from Starbucks, which contributes five cents from every bottle sold to water-purification centres in developing countries.”
他的例子是 Starbucks 的 Ethos Water；每賣出一瓶，就會捐出五美分給發展中國家的淨水中心。
題目中的 “helps provide money for” 對應原文 “contributes five cents from every bottle sold to…”。答案需要概括資金去向。
“water-purification centres” 指淨水中心，也就是 clean water projects。選項 C 最貼近。

A poor people in Africa：原文說 developing countries，沒有只限 Africa，也沒有說直接給 poor people。 B poor farmers：Fair Trade coffee 和 farmer pay 出現在其他段落，Ethos Water 的例子不涉及農民。 C clean water projects：正確，對應 “water-purification centres”。答案是 C。

questions.translation: Joe Curnow 最初透過購買甚麼參與 consumer activism？

blocks.text: “Joe Curnow first got involved with consumer activism through buying…”
便利性也正在推動消費者 activism。
“When the tally reached $8,000, they realised they were striking a chord.”
當銷售總額達到 8,000 美元時，她們意識到自己引起了共鳴。
這段講 consumer activism 的便利性，以及青少年如何用購買或販賣 Fair Trade products 參與行動。Joe Curnow 是段落前半的人物。
“Joe Curnow, national coordinator of United Students for Fair Trade, says she first got involved about five years ago as a high schooler when she spent time hanging out in cafes.”
United Students for Fair Trade 的全國協調員 Joe Curnow 說，她大約五年前還是高中生時，常在 cafés 逗留，當時首次參與其中。
“Buying coffee with an eco-friendly label ‘was a very easy way for me to express what I believed in,’ she says.”
她說，購買貼有 eco-friendly 標籤的咖啡，是表達自己信念的一個非常簡單的方法。
題目問 “through buying” 甚麼。原文直接說：
A coffee：正確，原文直接重現。
B cocoa：Equal Exchange 推出 cocoa 是 Paragraph 4 的內容，不是 Joe Curnow 的個人經歷。
C water：Ethos Water 是 Michael Wood 的例子，人物不同。

questions.prompt: “Eighth-graders from Fayerweather Street School go to the natural-foods grocer’s rather than the 31 ______.”
questions.translation: Fayerweather Street School 的八年級學生去 natural-foods grocer’s，而不去 ______。

blocks.text: “When classes adjourn here at the Fayerweather Street School, eighth-graders ignore the mall down the street and go straight to the place they consider much cooler: the local natural-foods grocer’s.”
Fayerweather Street School 下課後，八年級學生無視街上的 mall，直接去他們覺得更酷的地方：本地 natural-foods grocer’s。
“‘Food is something you need to stay alive,’ says eighth-grader Emma Lewis.”
八年級學生 Emma Lewis 說：「食物是維持生命所需要的東西。」首句已直接回答題目，這段功能是用學生放學後的選擇引入 ethical food purchasing。
“go straight to … the local natural-foods grocer’s”
題目要求 NO MORE THAN ONE WORD。原文中學生 ignore 的地方是：
空格前已有 “the”，所以填單字： mall
go to the natural-foods grocer’s rather than the mall= ignore the mall and go straight to the natural-foods grocer’s答案是 mall。

questions.translation: Bon Appétit ______ 限制自己的增長。

blocks.text: “‘Prior to that, students were excited to be getting sugared cereal.’”
在那之前，學生只因得到含糖 cereal 而興奮。
這段講校園 food-service provider Bon Appétit 的增長，以及學生需求如何轉向 food source 和ethical produce。
“Though Bon Appétit intentionally limits its growth, its collegiate client list has grown from 58 to 71 in that period.”
雖然 Bon Appétit 有意限制自己的增長，但在那段期間，它的大學客戶名單由 58 增至 71。
題目句子需要一個副詞，修飾 “limits its growth”。原文完全對應：
所以答案是： intentionally注意 ONE WORD 限制。不要填 “its growth” 或 “limits its growth”。答案只需要副詞。

questions.prompt: “Previously, young generations were 33 ______ to make sacrifices.”
questions.translation: 以前的年輕世代受到 ______，願意作出犧牲。

blocks.text: “The concerns of today’s young food shoppers seem in some ways to reflect the idealism that inspired previous generations to join boycotts in solidarity with farm workers.”
今日年輕 food shoppers 的關注，在某些方面似乎反映了曾激勵上一代人參與 boycott、聲援farm workers 的理想主義。
“‘My generation has come to terms with the fact that we’re all consumers, and we all buy something. So, if I do have to buy food, what are the consequences?’”
「我這一代已經接受一個事實：我們都是消費者，我們都會買東西。所以，如果我必須買食物，會有甚麼後果？」這段比較 previous generations 和 today’s youthful consumers。題目有 Previously 和 sacrifices，所以定位到這段。
“The concerns of today’s young food shoppers seem in some ways to reflect the idealism that inspired previous generations to join boycotts in solidarity with farm workers.”
“Today’s efforts are distinct in that youthful consumers say they do not want to make sacrifices.”
今日的努力有其不同之處：年輕消費者說自己不想作出犧牲。
題目要填 ONE WORD，而且句型是：
題目把 “previous generations to join boycotts” 改寫為 “young generations were inspired to make sacrifices”。Boycotts 本身通常涉及不買某些產品，帶有犧牲便利或選擇的意味。下一句也用 “do not want to make sacrifices” 對比今日青年。
previous generations= young generations previously idealism inspired previous generations= young generations were inspired join boycotts= make sacrifices in activism context

questions.prompt: “Young people can feel frustrated and 34 ______ because of their age.”
questions.translation: 年輕人會因為年紀而感到沮喪和 ______。

blocks.text: “Wanting to ameliorate the world’s big problems can be frustrating, especially for those who feel ineffective because they are young.”
想改善世界的大問題可能令人沮喪，尤其是對那些因年輕而覺得自己沒有影響力的人。
“‘Buying products or supporting companies that give them ways to support global issues is one way for them to get involved, and they really appreciate that.’”
購買產品或支持能讓他們參與全球議題的公司，是一種參與方式；他們很欣賞這一點。
因為自己年輕而覺得沒有影響力。
“feel frustrated and ______ because of their age”
空格要填形容詞，且必須來自原文。答案是： ineffective
because of their age= because they are young frustrated= frustrating feel ineffective= feel unable to make a difference

questions.prompt: “Gary Lindsay 35 ______ people to buy products that make use of Fair Trade.”
questions.translation: Gary Lindsay ______ 人們購買使用 Fair Trade 的產品。

blocks.text: “Some adults hasten to point out the limitations of ethical consumption as a tool for doing good deeds and personal growth.”
一些成人急於指出 ethical consumption 作為行善和個人成長工具的限制。

“‘Those things are great when we’re given opportunities like that once in a while, but I think for us to expect that we should get something out of everything we do is a very selfish attitude to have.’”
「偶爾有這樣的機會時，那些東西很好；但我認為，如果我們期待自己做每件事都要得到某些東西，這是一種很自私的態度。」這段講 Gary Lindsay 對 Fair Trade purchases 的保留態度，但也說他支持這類購買。

“Gary Lindsay, director of Children’s Ministries, encourages Fair Trade purchases, but he also organises projects in which children collect toys for foster children and save coins for a playground-construction project in Tanzania.”
Children’s Ministries 的 director Gary Lindsay 鼓勵 Fair Trade purchases，但他也組織一些項目，讓孩子為寄養兒童收集玩具，並為 Tanzania 的 playground-construction project 儲零錢。
題目把名詞短語 “Fair Trade purchases” 改寫成 “people to buy products that make use of Fair Trade”。所以答案是： encourages注意字形：Gary Lindsay 是第三身單數，所以原文用 encourages，題目也需要同一形式。

questions.prompt: “Fair Trade coffee is more expensive than usual coffee.”
questions.translation: Fair Trade coffee 比普通 coffee 更貴。

blocks.text: “Eating morally, as some describe it, is becoming a priority for teenagers as well as adults in their early 20s.”
一些人稱之為「有道德地飲食」；這正成為青少年和二十出頭成年人重視的事情。
“Their peers on another 300 campuses are pushing to follow suit, according to Students United for Fair Trade in Washington, D.C.”
根據 Students United for Fair Trade，另有 300 個校園的同齡學生也正推動跟隨這種做法。
這段有 Fair Trade coffee，所以 Question 36 定位到這裡。

“Students at 30 colleges have helped persuade administrators to make sure all cafeteria coffee comes with a ‘Fair Trade’ label, which means bean pickers in Latin America and Africa were paid more than the prevailing rates.”
30 間 college 的學生已幫助說服管理層，確保所有 cafeteria coffee 都有 “Fair Trade” label；這表示 Latin America 和 Africa 的採豆工人得到高於 prevailing rates 的報酬。
“bean pickers … were paid more than the prevailing rates”
也就是採豆工人獲得高於一般水平的工資。題目問的是 coffee 的售價：
“Fair Trade coffee is more expensive than usual coffee.”
這需要原文提供消費者支付價格，並且把 Fair Trade coffee 和 usual coffee 比較。原文沒有說Fair Trade coffee 的售價，也沒有出現 “more expensive than usual coffee” 這種 price comparison。
不能用常識推理：工人得到更高報酬，所以咖啡一定更貴。IELTS Reading 需要文本證據。原文只支援「工人被付更高工資」，沒有支援「消費者買到的咖啡更貴」。

questions.prompt: “Bon Appétit used to sell sugared cereal.”
questions.translation: Bon Appétit 以前賣 sugared cereal。

blocks.text: “‘Prior to that, students were excited to be getting sugared cereal.’”
「在那之前，學生只因得到含糖 cereal 而感到興奮。」這段提到 Bon Appétit，也提到 sugared cereal，所以這題定位到 Paragraph 3。

“‘It’s really just been in the last five years that we’ve seen students become concerned with where their food was coming from,’ says Maisie Ganzler, Bon Appétit’s director of strategic initiatives. ‘Prior to that, students were excited to be getting sugared cereal.’”
Bon Appétit 的 strategic initiatives director Maisie Ganzler 說：「其實只是過去五年，我們才看到學生開始關心自己的食物來自哪裡。在那之前，學生只因得到含糖 cereal 而感到興奮。」
“Bon Appétit used to sell sugared cereal.”
這包含兩個核心元素：第一，Bon Appétit 曾經提供或銷售 sugared cereal。
“students were excited to be getting sugared cereal”
這句的主體是 students；動作是 getting，不是 Bon Appétit selling。雖然說話者是 Bon Appétit 的director，但這句沒有明確說 sugared cereal 是 Bon Appétit 賣的，也沒有說它是公司以前的產品或服務。
原文可以支持「學生以前關注點較低，只因拿到含糖 cereal 而開心」。它仍未提供「Bon Appétit used to sell sugared cereal」這個具體商業動作。

questions.prompt: “Hob Everts thinks that kids do not understand the importance of protecting the environment.”
questions.translation: Hob Everts 認為孩子不了解保護環境的重要性。

blocks.text: “To reach a younger set that often does not drink coffee, Fair Trade importer Equal Exchange rolled out a line of cocoa in 2003 and chocolate bars in 2004.”
為了接觸較年輕、常不喝 coffee 的群體，Fair Trade importer Equal Exchange 在 2003 年推出cocoa 系列，2004 年推出 chocolate bars。
「所以，這是一個成熟、合適的受眾。」這段講 younger set / kids 對 Fair Trade、recycling 和 eco-friendly practices 的接受度，Hob Everts 的看法就在這裡。
“‘Kids are often the ones who agitate in the family’ for recycling and other eco-friendly practices, Mr. Everts says.”
Everts 先生說：「孩子常常是在家庭中推動 recycling 和其他 eco-friendly practices 的人。」
題目說 Hob Everts 認為 kids do not understand the importance of protecting the environment。
原文方向相反。Everts 說孩子常常在家庭中 “agitate” for recycling and other eco-friendly practices。
“agitate for” 在這裡指積極推動、鼓吹、催促家人做某事。這表示孩子不只理解環保，還會主動推動家庭實踐環保行為。題目命題： kids do not understand environmental protection原文命題： kids often push family recycling and eco-friendly practices兩者方向衝突，所以答案是 FALSE。

questions.prompt: “Summer Rayne Oakes will wear clothes that do not look so good as long as they promote Fair Trade.”
questions.translation: Summer Rayne Oakes 只要衣服推廣 Fair Trade，即使不好看也會穿。

blocks.text: “The concerns of today’s young food shoppers seem in some ways to reflect the idealism that inspired previous generations to join boycotts in solidarity with farm workers.”
今日年輕 food shoppers 的關注，在某些方面似乎反映了曾激勵上一代人參與 boycott、聲援farm workers 的 idealism。
“‘My generation has come to terms with the fact that we’re all consumers, and we all buy something. So, if I do have to buy food, what are the consequences?’”
「我這一代已接受一個事實：我們都是消費者，我們都會買東西。所以，如果我必須買食物，會有甚麼後果？」這段講今日青年消費者不想犧牲品質、價格和外觀。Summer Rayne Oakes 的 quote 是關鍵證據。
“‘I’m not going to buy something that can’t stand on its own or looks bad just because it’s socially responsible,’ Ms. Oakes says.”
Oakes 女士說：「我不會只因為某件東西有社會責任，就買一件本身站不住腳或看起來很差的東西。」
題目說她會接受不好看的衣服，只要它們推廣 Fair Trade。原文明確排除這種態度：
中文意思是「看起來很差」。
中文意思是「只因為它有社會責任」。
所以她的態度是：ethical / socially responsible 不足以補償品質或外觀不佳。這和題目方向直接衝突。
題目命題：會買不好看的 socially responsible clothes原文命題：不會只因 socially responsible 就買不好看的東西所以答案是 FALSE。

questions.prompt: “Gary Lindsay thinks people should do more than just consume ethically.”
questions.translation: Gary Lindsay 認為人們不應只停留在 ethical consumption，也應做更多。

blocks.text: “Some adults hasten to point out the limitations of ethical consumption as a tool for doing good deeds and personal growth.”
一些成人急於指出 ethical consumption 作為行善和個人成長工具的限制。

“‘Those things are great when we’re given opportunities like that once in a while, but I think for us to expect that we should get something out of everything we do is a very selfish attitude to have.’”
「偶爾有這樣的機會時，那些東西很好；但我認為，如果期待自己做每件事都要得到某些東西，這是一種很自私的態度。」只看首尾句，Paragraph 8 是對 ethical consumption 的限制和補充。Gary Lindsay 的觀點就是： Fair Trade purchases 有價值，但不能成為唯一的行善方式。

“Gary Lindsay, director of Children’s Ministries, encourages Fair Trade purchases, but he also organises projects in which children collect toys for foster children and save coins for a playground-construction project in Tanzania.”
Gary Lindsay 鼓勵 Fair Trade purchases，但他也組織其他項目：孩子為寄養兒童收集玩具，並為 Tanzania 的 playground construction 儲零錢。
“He says it helps them learn to enjoy helping others even when they are not getting anything tangible in return.”
他說，這幫助孩子學會享受幫助別人，即使自己沒有得到任何有形回報。
題目說 Gary Lindsay 認為人們應該做 more than just consume ethically。原文支援這點：他 “encourages Fair Trade purchases”，表示他不反對 ethical consumption。
他 “also organises projects”，表示他還推動其他形式的幫助。
他強調孩子要學會 “helping others even when they are not getting anything tangible in return”，表示真正的行善不一定伴隨自己得到商品或好處。
“for us to expect that we should get something out of everything we do is a very selfish attitude”
若我們期待自己做每件事都要得到某些東西，這是一種很自私的態度。
consume ethically= Fair Trade purchases do more than just consume ethically= also organise toy collection / coin saving projects / help without tangible return所以答案是 TRUE。

paragraphOverview.title: Skim Roadmap：只看每段第一句和最後一句
paragraphOverview.intro: 先掌握每段的功能與主旨，再進入逐題定位和細讀分析。

paragraphs.summary: 第一句說 Fayerweather Street School 的八年級學生放學後不去 mall，反去 natural-foods grocer’s；最後一句由 Emma Lewis 說明 paying farmers well 很重要，否則生活會只剩 candy。只看首尾句，可以估計這段是全文引入：青少年把消費和道德選擇連在一起，連買 chocolate treat都會想到農民是否得到合理報酬。Question 31 會直接定位到這段。

第一句說 “Eating morally” 正成為 teenagers 和 early 20s adults 的 priority；最後一句說 300 個校園的學生也推動 Fair Trade coffee。只看首尾句，可以估計這段講 ethical purchasing 從校園擴散到 food and beverage industries。中間提到這股行動源自十年前避免購買 overseas sweatshops製造的 clothing。Question 27 和 Question 36 會在這段找到核心資訊。

第一句說 coffee 只是開始；Bon Appétit 使用 organic and locally grown produce；最後一句引用Maisie Ganzler，說以前學生只因得到 sugared cereal 而興奮。只看首尾句，可以估計這段講校園food-service 市場的改變：學生開始關心食物來源，Bon Appétit 因此吸引更多大學合作。 Question 28、32 和 37 都會定位到這段。

第一句說 Equal Exchange 為較年輕、常不喝 coffee 的群體推出 cocoa 和 chocolate bars；最後一句 Hob Everts 說 kids 是 ripe audience。只看首尾句，可以估計這段說 Fair Trade 從 coffee 擴展到 cocoa / chocolate，也說小孩常推動家庭做 recycling 和 eco-friendly practices。Question 38會定位到這段，因為題目問 Hob Everts 對 kids environmental understanding 的看法。

第一句說今日 young food shoppers 的關注，在某些方面反映上一代支持 farm workers boycotts的 idealism；最後一句 Summer Rayne Oakes 問：如果必須買食物，後果是甚麼？只看首尾句，可以估計這段比較昔日 boycott idealism 和今日 consumer activism。重點是今日青年不想犧牲品質、價格或外觀，也想避免剝削。Question 33 和 39 會用到這段。

第一句說年輕人想改善世界大問題，但常因年紀小而感到 frustrated；最後一句 Michael Wood 說支持有助 global issues 的公司，讓青年有方式參與，他們很欣賞這一點。只看首尾句，可以估計這段講 marketing 如何回應青少年的 powerlessness。中間用 Ethos Water 作例子：每瓶捐五美分給 developing countries 的 water-purification centres。Question 29 和 34 會定位到這段。

第一句說 convenience 也推動 consumer activism；最後一句說 Fayerweather 學生在校園fundraisers 賣 Fair Trade products，銷售達 $8,000 時發現自己引起共鳴。只看首尾句，可以估計這段講簡單、方便的消費如何成為青少年 activism 的第一步。Joe Curnow 的例子會回答Question 30：她最初是透過在 café 買 eco-friendly coffee 參與。
第一句說一些成人急於指出 ethical consumption 作為行善和個人成長工具的限制；最後一句Gary Lindsay 認為若期待每次行善都有所得，是很自私的態度。只看首尾句，可以估計這段是全文的保留觀點：Fair Trade purchases 有價值，但孩子也應學習沒有 tangible return 的幫助方式。 Question 35 和 Question 40 會定位到這段。
